items.answer:
Please refer to the paper \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16093}{ Multiple chordal SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Moser system }

\textbf{Partition functions and null vector equations.}  
Let $x_1,\dots,x_n\in\mathbb R$ be distinct boundary points.  
A smooth positive function $Z(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ is called a \emph{partition function} if it is Möbius covariant with boundary weight
\[
h=\frac{6-\kappa}{2\kappa},
\]
and for each $i=1,\dots,n$ satisfies the level-two null vector (BPZ) equation
\[
\frac{\kappa}{2}\,\partial_{x_i x_i} Z
+\sum_{k\neq i}\frac{2}{x_k-x_i}\,\partial_{x_k}Z
+\sum_{k\neq i}\frac{2h}{(x_k-x_i)^2}\,Z = 0.
\tag{$\star_i$}
\]

\medskip
\textbf{Commutation relations.}  

Given such a partition function $Z$, define for each $i$
\[
\mathcal L_i
= \frac{\kappa}{2}\,\partial_{x_i x_i}
+ \kappa\,(\partial_{x_i}\log Z)\,\partial_{x_i}
+ \sum_{k\neq i}\frac{2}{x_k-x_i}\,\partial_{x_k}.
\]

The operators $\mathcal L_i$ describe the infinitesimal evolution when a slit is grown at $x_i$.  

Probabilistically, commutation relations say that if one first grows the slit at $x_i$ for an infinitesimal time and then at $x_j$, or reverses the order, the resulting law of the configuration is the same (up to reparametrization).

Dub\'edat’s commutation theorem asserts that for all $i\neq j$,
\[
[\mathcal L_i,\mathcal L_j]
= \frac{4}{(x_j-x_i)^2}\,\bigl(\mathcal L_j - \mathcal L_i\bigr).
\]

\medskip
\textbf{Driving SDE formulation.}  
Under the probability measure determined by $Z$, the driving processes $(X_t^1,\dots,X_t^n)$ satisfy
\[
dX_t^i \;=\; \sqrt{\kappa}\,dB_t^i
+ \left(\kappa\,\partial_{x_i}\log Z(X_t)
+ \sum_{k\neq i}\frac{2}{X_t^i - X_t^k}\right)\,dt,
\qquad i=1,\dots,n,
\]
where $(B_t^i)_{i=1}^n$ are independent standard Brownian motions.  
The infinitesimal generator of the $i$-th coordinate is precisely $\mathcal L_i$, and the commutation relation shows that the joint law is independent of the order in which the curves are explored.

info.problem_name: Commutation relations for multiple chordal SLE
info.problem_statement: Please explain the commutation relations for multiple chordal SLE(κ).
info.standard_solution:
Please refer to the paper \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16093}{ Multiple chordal SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Moser system }

\textbf{Partition functions and null vector equations.}  
Let $x_1,\dots,x_n\in\mathbb R$ be distinct boundary points.  
A smooth positive function $Z(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ is called a \emph{partition function} if it is Möbius covariant with boundary weight
\[
h=\frac{6-\kappa}{2\kappa},
\]
and for each $i=1,\dots,n$ satisfies the level-two null vector (BPZ) equation
\[
\frac{\kappa}{2}\,\partial_{x_i x_i} Z
+\sum_{k\neq i}\frac{2}{x_k-x_i}\,\partial_{x_k}Z
+\sum_{k\neq i}\frac{2h}{(x_k-x_i)^2}\,Z = 0.
\tag{$\star_i$}
\]

\medskip
\textbf{Commutation relations.}  

Given such a partition function $Z$, define for each $i$
\[
\mathcal L_i
= \frac{\kappa}{2}\,\partial_{x_i x_i}
+ \kappa\,(\partial_{x_i}\log Z)\,\partial_{x_i}
+ \sum_{k\neq i}\frac{2}{x_k-x_i}\,\partial_{x_k}.
\]

The operators $\mathcal L_i$ describe the infinitesimal evolution when a slit is grown at $x_i$.  

Probabilistically, commutation relations say that if one first grows the slit at $x_i$ for an infinitesimal time and then at $x_j$, or reverses the order, the resulting law of the configuration is the same (up to reparametrization).

Dub\'edat’s commutation theorem asserts that for all $i\neq j$,
\[
[\mathcal L_i,\mathcal L_j]
= \frac{4}{(x_j-x_i)^2}\,\bigl(\mathcal L_j - \mathcal L_i\bigr).
\]

\medskip
\textbf{Driving SDE formulation.}  
Under the probability measure determined by $Z$, the driving processes $(X_t^1,\dots,X_t^n)$ satisfy
\[
dX_t^i \;=\; \sqrt{\kappa}\,dB_t^i
+ \left(\kappa\,\partial_{x_i}\log Z(X_t)
+ \sum_{k\neq i}\frac{2}{X_t^i - X_t^k}\right)\,dt,
\qquad i=1,\dots,n,
\]
where $(B_t^i)_{i=1}^n$ are independent standard Brownian motions.  
The infinitesimal generator of the $i$-th coordinate is precisely $\mathcal L_i$, and the commutation relation shows that the joint law is independent of the order in which the curves are explored.
